Name: Encoded PowerShell Command
BenignExplanation: Some legitimate deployment/management tooling wraps PowerShell commands in -EncodedCommand purely to avoid shell-quoting issues, not to evade detection. Cross-check the decoded content and the initiating process against known deployment tools before escalating.

Name: Suspicious Execution Path
BenignExplanation: Many legitimate installers, auto-updaters, and browser/app components execute from AppData, ProgramData, or Temp during normal operation. This rule is intentionally broad; pair it with a baseline/exclusion config for known-good software in your environment (see Test-MDEBaseline, build Phase 4).
Reference: MITRE ATT&CK T1036.005; SANS Hunt Evil poster

Name: AMSI Bypass Indicator
BenignExplanation: Legitimate security tooling and AMSI-related diagnostics can reference these same internals; verify the initiating process is not a known AV/EDR component before treating this as hostile.
Reference: MITRE ATT&CK T1562.001; publicly documented AMSI bypass techniques

Name: Defender Sensor Tampering (Registry)
BenignExplanation: Some organizations legitimately manage these settings via Group Policy or an approved AV/EDR management tool; check the initiating process against known configuration-management tooling before escalating.

Name: Certutil Decode Abuse (LOLBAS)
BenignExplanation: certutil -decode has legitimate uses in some certificate-management and scripting workflows; confirm the decoded output and initiating process before escalating.

Name: Registry Run Key Suspicious Target
BenignExplanation: Some legitimate applications (certain Electron-based apps, conferencing/collaboration tools) install to AppData and autostart from there; check the value name and vendor before escalating.

Name: Scheduled Task Creation
BenignExplanation: Scheduled task creation is routine in managed enterprise environments (SCCM, backup software, update mechanisms). This rule is intentionally broad; pair with a baseline/exclusion config for known task-creating tooling in your environment.

Name: LSASS Memory Dump Pattern
BenignExplanation: Authorized security testing or incident-response tooling can legitimately trigger this pattern; verify against approved engagement activity before treating as hostile.

Name: Registry Hive Save (SAM/SECURITY/SYSTEM)
BenignExplanation: Legitimate backup or system-migration tooling could theoretically do this, but rarely via a bare reg.exe save command; verify the initiating process and account.

Name: PsExec Service Artifact
BenignExplanation: PsExec is a legitimate, widely-used sysadmin tool; its presence alone does not establish malicious intent. Check whether the initiating account/host is expected admin tooling.

Name: WMI Remote Execution
BenignExplanation: wmic /node is also used by legitimate remote-management scripts, though less commonly than more mainstream admin tooling.

Name: Archive Staging Suspicious Path
BenignExplanation: Archive tools plus AppData/Temp paths are also extremely common for entirely benign reasons -- extracting a downloaded zip, temp working directories for legitimate business processes.

Name: Domain Trust Reconnaissance
BenignExplanation: IT/helpdesk staff and various legitimate AD management or monitoring scripts run this command routinely.
